item.title: Sanders Responds To Streamer Claim: Coach denies college offer to Rakai; praises teen’s effort
item.description: Deion Sanders reacted after streamer Rakai claimed the Colorado coach offered him a college football deal during NFL Pro Bowl weekend. In a Well Off Media video, Sanders praised Rakai’s effort but questioned whether he is a college athlete right now. The exchange sparked debate online and gave fans plenty to discuss.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Blackstone founder Stephen Schwarzman plans to donate his entire $48 billion fortune to a major philanthropic foundation
item.description: Blackstone co-founder Stephen Schwarzman is reportedly planning to transfer nearly his entire $48 billion fortune to his philanthropic foundation. This move could establish the Stephen A. Schwarzman Foundation as one of the world's largest charitable organizations. His focus will be on artificial intelligence, education, and preparing societies for technological shifts, building on his existing global initiatives.

item.title: US military strikes three alleged drug-trafficking boats, killing 11 people
item.description: US forces struck three vessels in the eastern Pacific and Caribbean. Eleven individuals on board were killed. These actions are part of a campaign that began in September. The US military previously justified lethal strikes against suspected drug traffickers. This approach contrasts with earlier law enforcement methods.

item.title: Did Kai Cenat unfollow Ray on Instagram? Social media move sparks fan speculation online
item.description: Rumors claimed Kai Cenat unfollowed Ray and ended their friendship, but available facts show otherwise. Kai still follows Ray online, and no official statement confirms any fallout. The story spread mainly through social media speculation. Ray even recently thanked Kai during Super Bowl weekend, suggesting their bond remains strong despite the online noise.

item.title: Jeffrey Epstein’s Zorro Ranch to be probed after unanimous vote by New Mexico lawmakers
item.description: New Mexico lawmakers have unanimously approved a probe into Jeffrey Epstein's Zorro Ranch, creating a special committee to investigate alleged criminal activity. This legislative action coincides with federal efforts to release Epstein-related information, as survivors claim abuse occurred at the ranch. Former state efforts to investigate were previously halted by federal prosecutors.

item.title: Explosion at New York church injures five; witnesses say they smelled gas odour before incident
item.description: An explosion rocked Abundant Life Fellowship Church in Boonville, New York. Five people were injured in the blast. First responders arrived after reports of a gas odor. A firefighter and one civilian are in critical condition. The church suffered catastrophic damage. Investigations are ongoing into the cause of the explosion.

item.title: Hate against Indians in US rose 115% in just two years as immigration debates intensified
item.description: Hate speech targeting Indians and South Asians surged between 2023-2025, fueled by immigration policy debates and online conspiracy narratives. Anti-South Asian slurs saw a 115% online increase, with content targeting Indians driving much of this rise. This trend, linked to H-1B visa discussions, is raising concerns about escalating hostility and potential offline discrimination.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists warn melting ice could release 5,000-year-old superbug that resists 10 modern antibiotics
item.description: Romanian scientists have revived a 5,000-year-old bacterium, Psychrobacter SC65A.3, from Scărișoara Ice Cave, revealing resistance to 10 modern antibiotics. The discovery highlights natural, ancient origins of antibiotic resistance and warns that melting ice could release genes into contemporary bacteria. At the same time, these cold-adapted microbes hold potential for new antibiotics, enzymes, and biotechnological innovations, underscoring both risk and opportunity.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Why did Larry Wheels slap DeenTheGreat during Kick livestream? Viral moment explained
item.description: A livestream featuring Larry Wheels, DeenTheGreat, and Rampage Jackson turned viral after a tense moment ended in a slap on February 16, 2026. The clip, shared widely on social media, showed rising tension during a conversation outside a restaurant. The incident sparked debate online while also bringing renewed attention to Larry Wheels’ fitness career and streaming presence.

item.title: Iran, US agree on ‘guiding principles’ in nuclear talks; Tehran cautions ‘not an agreement’
item.description: Iran and the United States have found common ground on key principles during nuclear talks in Geneva. While progress is noted, a final agreement is not yet in sight. Negotiations are expected to continue. The discussions occurred amidst heightened tensions in the Gulf region. Military drills were conducted by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: ‘Extremely disrespectful’: What is the ‘Captain Durag’ controversy all about? Explained
item.description: Disney Jr.'s "Hey AJ!" introduced "Captain Durag," a new superhero intended to celebrate Black culture, but the character has sparked controversy. Critics argue the portrayal leans into stereotypes, especially airing during Black History Month. The show's writer defended the character as a homage to Blaxploitation films and a challenge to respectability politics.

item.title: Husband catches Indiana school secretary having sex with a student
item.description: A school secretary in Union City, identified as Alicia Hughes, faces serious allegations of sexual relationships with two students. Authorities arrested Hughes, charging her with five counts of child seduction involving a 17-year-old. The investigation began after her husband reportedly discovered her with an 18-year-old student.
